channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Para 75% dos brasileiros, STF tem poder demais, diz Datafolha
item.description: According to a Datafolha poll, 75% of Brazilians believe the Supreme Federal Court (STF) has too much power, although 71% consider the Court essential for maintaining democracy. The perception of excessive power is higher among Jair Bolsonaro voters (88%) and lower among Lula supporters (64%). The survey also found that 70% of respondents were aware of suspicions linking STF ministers to the Master Case, of whom 55% believe the ministers are involved.

item.title: Na Presidência do TSE, Nunes Marques vai defender higidez e credibilidade das urnas
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques is set to be elected president of the TSE on Tuesday (14), succeeding Cármen Lúcia and beginning preparations for the 2026 elections. He pledges to personally defend the integrity of electronic voting machines, combat voter abstention, accelerate the removal of harmful AI-generated content, and increase Indigenous participation in the electoral process. André Mendonça will be elected vice-president, and both were nominated to the STF by Jair Bolsonaro, despite his history of unfounded attacks on the electoral system.

item.title: Nunes Marques chega ao comando do TSE prometendo perfil discreto e discurso de pacificação em ano eleitoral
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) is set to be elected president of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) this Tuesday, promising a discreet, impartial management aimed at reducing political tension in the election year. His appointment follows the early departure of Carmen Lucía, based on seniority, and he will oversee the full organization of the 2026 elections. Known for a low-friction profile and conservative rulings on moral and criminal guarantees, Nunes Marques avoids public confrontations, with André Mendonça as vice-president reinforcing the commitment to discretion and stability.

item.title: TSE retoma julgamento que pode cassar governador de Roraima e levar a novas eleições no estado
item.description: The TSE resumes the trial that could lead to the removal of Roraima's governor, Edilson Damião (Republicans), and trigger new elections in the state, in a case also involving former governor Antonio Denarium (PP). Both are accused of using social programs for electoral gain, transferring funds during prohibited periods, and misusing institutional advertising for personal promotion. Court ministers view the outcome as likely unfavorable, with risks of mandate removal and ineligibility.

item.title: Lula aconselhou Moraes sobre caso Master por respeitá-lo, diz PT
item.description: PT national president Edinho Silva stated that Lula advised Alexandre de Moraes to recuse himself in the Banco Master case out of respect for the minister, aiming to safeguard his legacy and ensure full investigation of allegations. Edinho praised Moraes for having 'fulfilled a magnificent role in defense of democracy' and denied any TCU-related deal or Paraíba candidacy agreement, confirming Lula's support for João Azevêdo and Veneziano Vital do Rêgo.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro lança programa em canal conservador no YouTube
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro announced a new weekly program on the Rede Comunica Brasil YouTube channel, set to premiere on April 14, 2026, at 7 a.m. Brasília time. The channel, based in Salvador and focused on Christian and family-oriented content, has 55,000 YouTube subscribers and 91,600 Instagram followers. The program will feature Bahia state deputy Leandro de Jesus (PL) and reflects Eduardo Bolsonaro’s continued reliance on video messaging following his self-exile in the United States since February 2025.

item.title: Deputados se juntam a Seif e pedem asilo político a Ramagem
item.description: Opposition lawmakers, led by Cabo Gilberto (PL), requested political asylum in the U.S. for Alexandre Ramagem, former Abin director and ex-deputy detained by ICE after his visa expired. They claim Ramagem is a political persecutee due to his STF conviction for involvement in the 2023 coup plot. Senator Jorge Seif had previously made the same request.

item.title: Pimenta protocola 3 projetos na estreia como líder de Lula na Câmara
item.description: The new government leader in the Chamber of Deputies, Paulo Pimenta (PT-RS), filed three bills on his first day in office, including regulations for electronic toll-free flow systems, the National Program for Autonomy and Protection of Women in Domestic Violence Situations ('Recomeçar Mulher'), and the 'Single Water Meter Law' to prevent commercial fees on mixed-use residential properties. He replaced José Guimarães as government leader after Guimarães was appointed to the Institutional Relations Secretariat.

item.title: Padilha associa Flávio Bolsonaro a ‘apagão’ em hospitais do RJ e diz que saúde será tema eleitoral
item.description: Health Minister Alexandre Padilha linked Flávio Bolsonaro to the mismanagement of federal hospitals in Rio de Janeiro, claiming the senator was responsible for a true 'blackout' in the state's health system and should not govern the country or the Ministry of Health. He stated that health will be a central theme in the 2026 elections, contrasting the current government's proposals with Bolsonaro's history of negationist stances on vaccination and international health cooperation. Padilha also reinforced Lula's support for Fernando Haddad as the winning candidate in São Paulo, emphasizing the state's decisive role in the 2022 presidential election.

item.title: Oposição no Brasil diz que vai pressionar por asilo a Ramagem nos EUA
item.description: The leader of the opposition in the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies, Cabo Gilberto (PL-PB), announced that the group will pressure the United States to grant political asylum to Alexandre Ramagem, a former deputy and Bolsonaro ally detained by immigration authorities in Orlando after losing his mandate and diplomatic passport. Ramagem has been a fugitive in the U.S. since September 2025, sentenced to 16 years by the STF for his role in the January 8 attacks, and already has an asylum request filed in the U.S., which the opposition seeks to prioritize.

item.title: Comissão da Câmara aprova 7 candidatos ao TCU; plenário vota nesta terça
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Finance and Taxation Committee unanimously approved seven candidates for the vacant TCU minister position left by Aroldo Cedraz's retirement. The final decision will be made in a secret ballot in the plenary on Tuesday, with the top vote-getter proceeding to a Senate hearing and vote. Odair Cunha (PT-MG) has the backing of Chamber President Hugo Motta and a coalition of parties including MDB, PT, PDT, PCdoB, PSB, and Republicanos.

item.title: União Brasil em São Paulo ameaça implodir federação com o PP
item.description: The São Paulo branch of União Brasil threatens to dissolve its federation with the PP if Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) is appointed as the alliance's leader, insisting that São Paulo politics demands local leadership and rejecting rule by proxy. The statement from party president Alexandre Leite warns that if reason does not prevail, the party will escalate the issue to the National Executive and work to permanently dismantle the alliance, causing instability in the electoral process.

item.title: Ramagem foi detido por infração de trânsito, diz Eduardo
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro stated that Alexandre Ramagem was detained in the U.S. for a traffic violation, not due to Brazil's extradition request. Ramagem, who has been a fugitive since his conviction for involvement in the coup attempt, is awaiting an asylum hearing in the U.S., with strong expectations of release. Paulo Figueiredo, an ally and partner at Immigrex, confirmed he is providing legal assistance to prevent deportation.

item.title: “Isso vai acabar”, diz Flávio ao comentar prisão de Ramagem
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) commented on the arrest of Alexandre Ramagem by ICE in Orlando, Florida, stating that the former deputy has an ongoing asylum request and is legally well-protected. Flávio said 'this will end', expressing confidence in the reversal of the measure. The statement was posted on X (formerly Twitter).

item.title: Após pressão do governo, projeto que regulamenta atividade de entregadores e motoristas sai de pauta na Câmara
item.description: The bill regulating app-based delivery and ride-hailing workers was removed from the Chamber of Deputies' agenda following government pressure, with rapporteur Augusto Coutinho declaring the project 'dead'. The proposal set a minimum of R$8.50 per delivery or R$14.74 per hour, but faced opposition from Minister Guilherme Boulos (PSOL), who advocated for R$10 per trip, and resistance from platforms and workers, resulting in its withdrawal.

item.title: Amigo de Lula, Emílio Odebrecht é apontado como fornecedor de carne de paca servida por Janja na Páscoa
item.description: A longtime friend of President Lula, Emilio Odebrecht, was identified as the supplier of paca meat served by Janja at Easter, according to an O Globo report. Odebrecht claims to be Brazil’s largest paca breeder and allegedly gifted the meat to the presidential couple. While no illegality is suggested, the connection raises concerns about potential conflicts of interest given Odebrecht’s historical ties to the Lula administration.

item.title: Lula vê evaporar vantagem sobre concorrentes em pesquisa Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows President Lula has lost his lead over rivals in the 2026 elections, entering a technical tie in various second-round scenarios. For the first time, he is numerically surpassed by Flávio Bolsonaro, with 46% voting intention versus 45% for the petista. Against Ronaldo Caiado and Romeu Zema, Lula also scores 45%, while opponents maintain similar percentages.

item.title: Cláudio Castro diz que não irá depor à CPI do Crime Organizado por ‘lombalgia aguda’
item.description: Former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro (PL) announced he will not appear before the Senate's Organized Crime CPI due to a diagnosis of acute lumbar pain, which requires him to avoid travel and in-person activities. The summons was approved after his resignation in March, as the STF had previously ruled that sitting governors cannot be summoned to CPI hearings. Castro was declared ineligible until 2030 by the TSE and is accused of using state agencies to create over 27,000 irregular appointed positions to benefit political allies and support his 2022 re-election bid.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia diz que é aconselhada a deixar o STF por ataques machistas
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia of the STF revealed that her family advises her to leave the position due to daily misogynistic and sexist attacks she endures. She noted that the hostile environment against women in the Court is so severe that some judges may refuse to join the Supreme Court out of fear of becoming targets. Despite the pressure, she insists she acts strictly within the law, while her family urges her to step down, saying she has already fulfilled her duty.

item.title: PF investiga governador de Roraima como chefe de esquema de fraudes
item.description: The Federal Police is investigating Roraima's governor, Edilson Damião (União Brasil), as the suspected leader of a fraud scheme in state infrastructure contracts, directing tenders to specific companies like C B Pedra Serviços e Construções and leaking bid results to allies before official publication. The probe also identifies former Civil Affairs chief Disney Barreto Mesquita as the head of the scheme's 'financial arm', allegedly laundering money through fuel stations and hotels. Damião assumed office in March 2026 after Antonio Denarium resigned to run for Senate, and both will face trial at the TSE on April 14 for abuse of power in the 2022 elections.

item.title: União Brasil em SP critica articulação para Ciro Nogueira liderar federação com PP e fala em risco de ruptura
item.description: The São Paulo branch of União Brasil opposed the proposal for Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) to lead the upcoming União Progressista federation, stating that leadership must reflect local realities. The party criticized negotiations with the PP as potentially covert and warned it would escalate the issue to the National Executive if unresolved, to prevent instability in the 2026 electoral project.

item.title: Lula troca chefe do INSS com 2,8 mi na fila da aposentadoria
item.description: Lula dismissed INSS president Gilberto Waller after the backlog of pension and benefit requests reached 2.79 million in March 2026, peaking at 3.13 million in February. His replacement, career official Ana Cristina Viana Silveira, is tasked with accelerating benefit analysis and simplifying internal processes to fulfill government promises of clearing the queue. Although the backlog fell 11% in March, it remains 156.8% higher than in December 2022, highlighting ongoing strain on the public pension system.

item.title: Com Lula contra, relator pede adiamento de análise de regulamentação de apps
item.description: The rapporteur of the bill regulating app-based work, Deputy Augusto Coutinho, requested the postponement of the bill's analysis in the special committee after the Lula government expressed disagreement with the latest version of the report. Although the topic is considered a priority by the government, Lula's allies advised the government base to vote against the bill, prompting Coutinho to seek House President Hugo Motta to avoid the vote. The rapporteur argued that postponement preserves the technical merit of the proposal, which includes rights such as algorithmic transparency, social security, and tax exemptions for vehicle purchases.

item.title: Leite apoia Caiado, mas rejeita “simples adesão”
item.description: Rio Grande do Sul Governor Eduardo Leite (PSD) said he respects his party's choice of Ronaldo Caiado as a presidential pre-candidate but rejected the notion that his support is merely a 'simple adherence,' stressing that his contribution must be more substantial.

item.title: Lula regulamenta reembolso-creche e redução de jornada para terceirizados do serviço público
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed acts regulating childcare reimbursement and expanding access to a reduced workweek of 40 hours (down from 44) for outsourced public service workers. The measure aims to improve working conditions and support work-life balance, particularly for parents.

item.title: 'Mera questão migratória', diz Flávio sobre prisão de Ramagem
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro described the arrest of Alexandre Ramagem by ICE as a 'mere migration issue', stating that the former deputy has an ongoing asylum petition and is expected to be released soon. He also signaled support for amnesty for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, claiming Brazil will no longer have political prisoners by 2027. The detention followed a traffic stop in Orlando, Florida, due to alleged immigration violations, unrelated to Ramagem’s STF conviction in Brazil.

item.title: Queda de veto do PL da Dosimetria beneficia presos por tráfico e feminicídio, diz estudo
item.description: Congress overturned the presidential veto on the Dosimetry Bill, a proposal that reduces sentences for heinous crimes such as drug trafficking and femicide. A study indicates the change directly benefits inmates convicted of these offenses, raising concerns among public safety experts.

item.title: Imprensa estrangeira repercute prisão de Ramagem pelo ICE e destaca fim de 'busca internacional de seis meses'
item.description: The international press reported on Monday the arrest of former Brazilian deputy Alexandre Ramagem by U.S. ICE agents, ending a six-month international manhunt across two continents. Ramagem was previously convicted by Brazil's Supreme Court for conspiring to overturn Bolsonaro's election loss and for turning the intelligence agency (Abin) into a clandestine unit to illegally monitor political opponents. outlets like The Washington Post, The Guardian, and Le Monde emphasized his flight to the U.S. before sentencing and his claim of having Trump administration approval.

item.title: Tarcísio de Freitas anuncia investimento milionário contra catástrofes climáticas em SP
item.description: The government of Tarcísio de Freitas announced an investment of 110 million reais in eight new weather radars in partnership with USP and SP Águas, expanding São Paulo's climate monitoring network. The announcement, scheduled for Tuesday (14), takes place during the 50th anniversary celebration of São Paulo's Civil Defense and includes a total package of about 195 million reais in disaster prevention measures, such as infrastructure projects, water trucks, and firefighting vehicles.

item.title: Alexandre Ramagem, ex-diretor da Abin de Bolsonaro, é preso nos EUA
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem, former head of Brazil's Abin intelligence agency under Jair Bolsonaro and sentenced to 16 years in prison by the STF for his role in the coup plot, was arrested in the United States for being in the country illegally. The arrest took place in Orlando by ICE agents, following international cooperation with Brazil's Federal Police. The detention may be used politically against Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 presidential campaign.

item.title: Escala 6x1: Lula marca encontro com Motta antes de enviar projeto do governo à Câmara
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will lunch with Chamber President Hugo Motta to explain the sending of a bill that ends the 6x1 work scale and reduces working hours. The bill will be sent under urgency regime, which locks Congress’s agenda until it is analyzed. Boulos confirmed the text is ready and only awaits the Lula-Motta meeting to be forwarded.

item.title: Comissão aprova sete candidatos ao TCU; votação secreta no Plenário ocorre nesta terça-feira
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies' Finance and Taxation Committee unanimously approved seven candidates for the TCU minister vacancy left by the retirement of Aroldo Cedraz. The final secret vote will take place in the Plenary this Tuesday, with the top candidate forwarded to Senate hearings and voting. Candidates were questioned on budget transparency, the 'secret budget,' and salary caps, notably Odair Cunha and Danilo Forte emphasizing technical independence and rigorous oversight.

item.title: Pimenta nega atrito entre Motta e Lula por PL do fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: The new government leader in the Chamber, Deputy Paulo Pimenta (PT-RS), denied that sending a constitutional urgency bill to end the 6x1 work schedule would create tensions between the Planalto and Chamber President Hugo Motta. He said Lula will meet with Motta before submitting the bill to ensure priority processing, given the electoral year, as the urgency regime allows only 45 days for Congress to vote before the agenda is locked.

item.title: Zema defende a prisão dos ‘intocáveis’ Alexandre de Moraes e Dias Toffoli
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) called for the imprisonment of Supreme Court justices Alexandre de Moraes and Dias Toffoli, labeling them 'untouchables' and accusing the STF of moral decay. He linked the judiciary's actions to a purported 'party of the untouchables' under Lula's government and cited a Datafolha poll showing him trailing Lula by 3 points in a hypothetical runoff.

item.title: Não tem o menor sentido haver só 1 dia de descanso, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula advocated for reducing the workweek to 40 hours with two days of rest, calling the 6x1 schedule senseless given technological advances. He announced an urgent bill to Congress to extend the benefit to all Brazilian workers, preserving salaries and avoiding the need for a constitutional amendment. The policy, already implemented for federal public sector outsourced workers, includes childcare reimbursement and reduced hours, benefiting around 60,000 people.

item.title: A resposta da defesa de Bolsonaro aos questionamentos de Moraes sobre irmão de Michelle
item.description: The defense of Jair Bolsonaro submitted a response to the STF addressing Minister Alexandre de Moraes' inquiries regarding the admission of Michelle's brother, Eduardo Torres, into the residence where the former president serves house arrest. The lawyers argued that Eduardo is not a health professional but a trusted family member necessary to assist Michelle in caring for Bolsonaro, citing his role in preparing meals at Papudinha and his pre-candidacy for federal deputy in DF under the PL. Moraes had required proof of technical qualifications to authorize the visit, as only close family, doctors, and lawyers are currently permitted.

item.title: União Brasil em SP rechaça comando de federação com o PP por Ciro Nogueira
item.description: The São Paulo branch of União Brasil rejected the possibility of Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) presiding over the party's federation with PP in the state, calling the proposal unacceptable and an attack on local leadership. State president Alexandre Leite stated the party will not accept being governed by outsiders and warned it may sabotage the alliance or escalate the issue to the National Executive if its demands are not met.

item.title: Ramagem disse estar seguro nos EUA antes de ser detido
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem, former federal deputy stripped of his mandate by the STF for involvement in the 2022 coup plot, stated in a November 2025 interview that he was 'safe' in the U.S. with the knowledge and consent of the American government, five months before being detained by ICE. He fled Brazil after a 16-year prison sentence, using a diplomatic passport and claiming to protect his family, while advocating amnesty for coup plotters and denouncing STF rulings as illegal.

item.title: Em gesto ao governo, Alcolumbre deve ir à posse de novo ministro da coordenação política
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) is expected to attend the swearing-in of José Guimarães (PT-CE) as the new Minister of Institutional Relations on Tuesday (14) at the Planalto Palace. The gesture is seen as a sign of institutional alignment between the Legislative and Executive branches.

item.title: Terceirizados do governo têm redução de jornada e auxílio para creche
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed measures expanding labor rights for federal outsourced workers, including a reduction of the workweek from 44 to 40 hours without salary reduction and a childcare reimbursement of up to R$ 526.64 per dependent per month. The policy covers approximately 40,000 workers and up to 14,000 children under six, matching benefits given to federal civil servants. Lula stressed the dignity and equality of these measures, highlighting the essential role of these workers following the January 8, 2023, attacks.

item.title: Oposição tenta unificar candidaturas de direita ao TCU e Motta pressiona por voto em petista
item.description: The opposition is attempting to unify six right-wing candidacies for the TCU vacancy to block the election of petista Odair Cunha, backed by Chamber President Hugo Motta. Motta has been lobbying lawmakers to vote for Odair to honor a 2024 agreement with the PT. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and influencer Pablo Marçal (União Brasil) are leading efforts to consolidate a single right-wing candidate, with Marçal pressuring rivals to withdraw and Bolsonaro coordinating meetings with deputies.

item.title: Zema se apresenta como “direita sem corrupção”
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and Novo party candidate, positioned himself as a 'corruption-free' right-wing alternative, distinguishing himself from sectors of the right involved in irregularities. He criticized the Liberal Party (PL), the party of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, implying that part of the right is compromised by illicit practices. Zema aimed to consolidate his image as an ethical option within the conservative spectrum.

item.title: Ramagem foi detido após infração de trânsito e deve ser liberado, diz Eduardo Bolsonaro
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem, former head of Brazil’s intelligence agency (Abin) and ally of Jair Bolsonaro, was detained in the U.S. over an alleged traffic violation, according to Eduardo Bolsonaro, who says Ramagem has legal immigration status and is awaiting an asylum hearing. The detention was confirmed by ICE and linked by the Federal Police to international cooperation, with Ramagem considered a fugitive for armed criminal organization and attempted coup. While allies claim it was a traffic offense, experts warn the detention could lead to deportation or advance Brazil’s extradition request, which has been pending since December 2023.

item.title: “Nem Trump está protegendo bolsonaristas”, diz Dirceu sobre Ramagem
item.description: Former minister José Dirceu (PT) criticized the lack of U.S. protection for Bolsonarists following the arrest of Alexandre Ramagem by ICE for illegally residing in the United States. Ramagem, sentenced to 16 years for his role in the January 8 coup attempt, was detained in Orlando due to cooperation between Brazilian and U.S. authorities. Dirceu stated that the coup attempt will not go unpunished.

item.title: Obra do túnel Santos-Guarujá pode começar em 2026, diz Alckmin
item.description: Vice President Geraldo Alckmin announced that construction of the Santos-Guarujá tunnel could begin in 2026, with completion expected by 2030, following a R$ 2.5 billion credit contract signed by Banco do Brasil with the São Paulo state government. The project, already environmentally licensed and awarded to Mota-Engil, faces criticism of the prior administration for withholding funds and a federal-state funding dispute, despite the TCU raising concerns about federal fund oversight.

item.title: Justiça suspende votação da reforma do estatuto do Corinthians
item.description: A Brazilian court suspended the Corinthians general assembly scheduled for April 18 to vote on the club’s statute reform, following an injunction by Judge Luis Fernando Nardelli in response to a petition by councilor Felipe Ezabella, who cited procedural irregularities. The reform proposed expanding the electoral college, granting voting rights to fans, and potentially converting the club into a soccer corporation (SAF). The suspension comes amid internal conflict, including the contested removal of Council President Romeu Tuma Júnior, which was approved by councilors in March but not yet judicially confirmed.

item.title: As articulações da PF para prender Ramagem nos EUA
item.description: Alexandre Ramagem, former head of Brazil's intelligence agency (Abin) and former federal deputy, was arrested in Orlando, Florida, by U.S. immigration authorities after months of coordination between Brazilian Federal Police and U.S. officials. The arrest aimed to bypass potential rejection of Brazil's extradition request related to his 16-year sentence for crimes tied to the January 8, 2023, attacks. Ramagem was detained over alleged immigration violations, with the goal of deporting him to Brazil to serve his sentence.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes quer reforço na sua ‘bancada’ do STF
item.description: Gilmar Mendes is seeking to strengthen his bloc on the Supreme Federal Court (STF) with the potential appointment of Jorge Messias, the Union’s Attorney General, to consolidate a pro-government majority and counter pressures from the Master case. The move reflects a political strategy to secure favorable rulings, particularly on supplementary elections and state succession, backed by allies like Moraes, Zanin, and Dino. Messias would be positioned as a loyal ally to both President Lula and Mendes, reinforcing the so-called 'xandônico bloc'.

item.title: Medidas para endividamento sairão depois da viagem de Lula, diz Durigan
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said relief measures for household indebtedness, including the new Desenrola Brasil program, will be announced after President Lula’s Europe trip ends on April 21. The program aims to renegotiate debts for over 80 million delinquent borrowers and may include restrictions on betting access to prevent re-indebtedness. Durigan will accompany Lula in Spain and Germany, focusing on economic and technological cooperation.

item.title: Vídeo: ‘Flávio Bolsonaro será o próximo presidente do Brasil’, diz Ricardo Nunes
item.description: São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB) stated that Flávio Bolsonaro will be the next president of Brazil, citing widespread rejection of Lula due to fiscal irresponsibility and poor economic management. He also pledged full support for Tarcísio de Freitas’ re-election bid in São Paulo and criticized former ally Simone Tebet, advocating for the MDB to remain independent in the 2026 presidential race.
